authoring.value: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{5}{y}\,i-\frac{5}{x}\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ Interpret circulation as the sum of the four convergent improper line integrals over the open quadrant arcs, taking independent one-sided limits at $(0,\pm1)$ and $(\pm1,0)$. Equivalently, integrate the continuous extension of the scalar pullback $F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)$. The field itself remains undefined at the four axis intersections, so the original ordinary circulation is undefined.
authoring.rationale: Separately reviewed explicit improper-integral correction. Authentic same-topic singular-field grades support the expected source key only; their unqualified ordinary prompts remain mathematically invalid. This correction independently makes the request well-posed.

authoring.value:
The field is undefined where $x=0$ or $y=0$, and the unit circle passes through four such points. Thus the original ordinary circulation is undefined. Under the stated improper-integral convention, the given parameterization is clockwise and

$$r(t)=(\sin t,\cos t),\qquad r\prime(t)=(\cos t,-\sin t).$$

On each open quadrant arc, both coordinates are nonzero, so

$$F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)=\frac{5}{\cos t}\cos t+\left(-\frac{5}{\sin t}\right)(-\sin t)=10.$$

Every one-sided endpoint limit of this scalar pullback is $10$. Each arc integral converges absolutely, independently of the other arcs. With $a_k=k\pi/2$,

$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{imp}}=\sum_{k=0}^{3}\lim_{\epsilon_k\downarrow0,\,\delta_k\downarrow0}\int_{a_k+\epsilon_k}^{a_{k+1}-\delta_k}10\,dt=4(5\pi)=20\pi.$$

This also equals the integral of the scalar pullback extended continuously by $10$ at its missing points. Only the scalar pullback is extended; the vector field is not assigned finite limits there. No principal-value cancellation or application of Green's theorem is needed.
